description: Nicolaas Maesstraat 47-61 (1910): 6.1-6.6 m brown-red brick fronts of four storeys under a flat roof behind a 1 m brick parapet with a stone coping; three axes of white T-windows under eared stone lintel slabs; iron-railed balconies on bracketed slabs on the centre axis of storeys 1 and 2; a double house door with a transom on an end axis

match.note: Nicolaas Maesstraat 51 on the 2024-12-11 strip (40 px/m, 1 m grid): storeys to 13.65 m, a brick parapet with recessed panels to its coping at 14.65 m; 3DBAG eaves 13.9-14.1 m read the roof edge behind the parapet. BAG 1910, widths 6.1-6.6 m; the strip skyline reads the parapet coping, 14.4-14.6 m on 47-61 (frontSkylineM)

parapet.note: Nicolaas Maesstraat 47-61: a brick parapet 13.65-14.65 m with three recessed panels and a stone coping (the panels are not drawn)

door-right.note: Nicolaas Maesstraat 51: a double house door with a transom on the right axis, two windows; the left-door houses (49, 53, 57, 61) are this front mirrored (match.mirrorForDoor)

roof.evidence: Nicolaas Maesstraat 47-61 (2024-12-11 strip): sky over the parapet coping on every pand; 3DBAG roof parts over 55 sit behind the parapet, out of the street view

rhythm.identicalBays: every upper storey: three T-windows of one width (1.2 m) under eared stone lintels
rhythm.symmetry: upper storeys symmetric; the door on the left or right axis
rhythm.groundFloor: residential: a double house door with a transom and two windows
rhythm.roofline: flat roof behind a 1 m brick parapet with a stone coping at 14.65 m
